      Three loops, one agent

      How it thinks.

      Each mechanic gets a dedicated module instead of one impossible end-to-end network.

      VISION + SLAM01

      Localise & map the world

      A RetinaNet detector finds NPCs, houses, gyms, Pokécenters, marts and exits in every frame. Odometry lifts those boxes onto a global tile map, which is far easier than reading the ROM's RAM.

      • CNN
      • object detection
      • mapper.py
      ROBOTICS02

      Explore with frontiers

      Boundary tiles between known and unknown space are scored by their neighbours. A BFS finds the best frontier, another BFS finds the path, and collisions trigger a replan.

      • frontier-based
      • BFS
      • path_finder.py
      REINFORCEMENT03

      Learn the battle

      A deep Q-network learns which of four moves wins more often. The reward is simple: damage dealt minus damage taken over a turn. It trains live in this page, with experience replay and a target network.

      • DQN
      • experience replay
      • online training

      Origin story

      Built for the love of Emerald.

      poke.AI began as an Orbital 2019 project at the NUS School of Computing and took home the Judge's Choice award. It is deliberately honest about the state of the art: general game-playing agents are still far from the fiction, so the project splits the problem into tidy, inspectable pieces.

      The long-term idea is simple. Give the agent eyes, a memory, curiosity and a little reinforcement learning — then let it wander Hoenn.
